title: Law Student Recruiting Moves Earlier as Employer-Sponsored Hiring Expands, New Report Finds (Perspectives on 2025 Law Student Recruiting)
author: NALP (National Association for Law Placement)

dom.t: Graduate hiring: Strong outcomes mask entry contraction

st.t: Graduate hiring: Strong outcomes mask entry contraction
st.an: NALP supports the synthesis’s distinction between entry-level contraction and continued pipeline strength: summer classes and per-office offers shrank, while aggregate offer volume remained nearly flat and post-graduation offer rates stayed high. It also confirms that recruiting moved markedly earlier and became predominantly employer-led.
qs: Key Findings:  Summer 2025 Programs and Outcomes     •   Nationally, the average number of 2L summer associates per individual office was eight in        2025, down from nine in 2024, and 10 in 2022 and 2023.
•   The offer rate from 2L summer programs (to return post-graduation as an entry-level        associate at the firm) held steady at 97%, unchanged from 2024.

kp.k: Employer-sponsored recruiting dominates the 2L hiring pipeline
kp.d: NALP reports that employer-sponsored recruiting generated 80% of offers during the 2025 recruiting cycle for 2026 2L summer programs, versus 20% through law-school-sponsored recruiting. Direct application was the most frequently cited recruitment method for the second consecutive year, used by 93% of offices, followed by law school recruitment programs at 71% and resume collects at 64%. These are legal recruitment findings; the release does not attribute them to AI.
qs: Overall, 80% of the offers made for 2026 2L summer programs resulted from employer sponsored recruiting and 20% resulted from law school sponsored recruiting.

For the second year in a row, direct application was the most frequently cited method by law offices to recruit 2L students (93%), followed by law school recruitment programs (e.g., OCI) at 71%, and resume collects (64%).

kp.d: The share of offers extended before July rose from 34% in 2024 to 85% in 2025. May accounted for 36% of offers, June for 29%, and April for 15%. Timing differed by channel: 65% of employer-sponsored offers were extended in May or earlier, whereas June was the most popular month for law-school-sponsored offers, accounting for 42%.
qs: In 2025, 85% of all offers were extended prior to July, compared to 34% of all offers in 2024.
May 2025 was the most popular offer month (36%), followed by June (29%), and then April (15%).

Offers that resulted from employer sponsored recruiting were commonly extended in May 2025 or earlier (65% of offers made via this method), while June was the most popular timeframe to extend offers that resulted from law school sponsored recruiting (42%).

kp.k: Earlier employer recruiting pressures first-year legal education
kp.d: NALP Executive Director Nikia Gray interprets the 2025 cycle as retaining the previous year's three-phase structure while moving the entire process materially earlier. She argues that employer recruiting activity is exerting significant pressure on the first-year curriculum and suggests widening pipelines as a possible response for employers seeking to escape accelerated competition. These are Gray's interpretation and recommendation, rather than measured curricular outcomes.
qs: The 2025 cycle not only reaffirmed the three-phase structure seen last year, but it also pulled the entire process materially forward.

It should give us pause that, in a period already defined by significant institutional change and disruption, one of the forces exerting the most pressure on the structure of the first-year curriculum is not pedagogical reform or accreditation standards, but employer recruiting activity.
For employers seeking exit ramps from this race to the bottom, widening pipelines may be the most effective lever available.

kp.k: Reporting categories changed alongside school recruitment schedules
kp.d: The 2024 survey separated OCI, early interview programs and recruitment outside school interview programs. Because some schools moved traditional OCI into spring or early summer in 2025, the new survey groups outcomes by who coordinates recruitment: law schools or employers. The release also qualifies its office-level reporting: some firms supplied firm-wide or multi-office data instead.
qs: As some law schools shifted their traditional OCI programs to the spring or early summer in 2025, this year’s survey streamlines outcomes into two primary categories: law school sponsored and employer sponsored recruiting defined below.
This includes any method for students to interview for 2L summer employment that is coordinated by a law school, group of law schools, or law student organizations, including OCI.
This includes any method for students to apply and interview for 2L summer employment that is coordinated by an employer.
Firms provided office-level data to the extent possible within the survey, but in some instances, firms were only able to provide firm-wide or multi-office data.

kp.k: Summer associate classes contracted at the office level
kp.d: The national average 2L summer class fell to eight per office in 2025, from nine in 2024 and 10 in both 2022 and 2023. NALP describes this as the smallest average since pandemic-disrupted 2020. New York City had the largest geographic-market average, at 29 students per office.
qs: Nationally, the average number of 2L summer associates per individual office was eight in 2025, down from nine in 2024, and 10 in 2022 and 2023.
This is the smallest average 2L class size per office since 2020, when many firms canceled or scaled back their programs due to the pandemic.
By geographic market, New York City had the largest class sizes, with an average of 29 2L students per office during summer 2025.

kp.k: Post-graduation offers remained high for 2L summer associates
kp.d: Despite smaller average summer classes, the offer rate for returning as an entry-level associate after graduation remained at 97%, unchanged from 2024. Acceptance was 89.4%, slightly below the 2024 record of 89.6%, and exceeded 89% for the fourth consecutive year.
qs: The offer rate from 2L summer programs (to return post-graduation as an entry-level associate at the firm) held steady at 97%, unchanged from 2024.
For the fourth year in a row, the offer acceptance rate exceeded 89%.
The 2025 rate was 89.4%, down just slightly from the record high of 89.6% in 2024.

kp.k: 1L return offers increased while acceptance declined
kp.d: Offers to 1L summer associates to return for summer 2026 reached an all-time high of 94.2%, increasing by 3.5 percentage points. Acceptance fell three percentage points to 72.3%. Among 1Ls accepting a 2L return offer, 75% would spend the entire 2026 summer with that firm, down from 79% during the previous summer.
qs: The offer rate to 1L summer associates (to return for the 2L 2026 summer program) increased by 3.5 percentage points to 94.2%, an all-time high.
The acceptance rate for those offers declined by three percentage points, dropping to 72.3%.
Overall, 75% of 1Ls who accepted a 2L summer return offer will spend the entire 2026 summer with their firm, down from 79% during the previous summer.

kp.k: Some offices bundled first- and second-year summer offers
kp.d: A new survey item measured 'jumbo offers': simultaneous offers covering both a student's 1L and 2L summers. During recruitment for summer 2025 1L and summer 2026 2L programs, 10% of offices with a 1L program made at least one such offer. Among those offices, 87% provided a bonus or another financial incentive to encourage acceptance of the 2L component.
qs: A new item was added to the 2025 survey to capture the prevalence of jumbo offers, which are offers extended simultaneously to a first-year student for employment during both their 1L and 2L summers.
During the 2025 recruiting cycle (for 1L summer 2025/2L summer 2026 programs), 10% of offices with a 1L summer program made at least one jumbo offer.
Of those offices that made jumbo offers, 87% offered a bonus or other financial incentive to encourage acceptance of the 2L portion of the offer.

kp.k: Callback conversion fell as offer acceptance reached records
kp.d: For summer 2026 positions, 47% of callbacks resulted in offers, down two percentage points from the preceding cycle. NALP reports that offer rates have remained below the 2014–2022 historical range of 50–58% since 2023. Acceptance rose three percentage points to a record 52%, the third consecutive record year, restoring the usual inverse relationship between offer and acceptance rates after its 2024 deviation.
qs: In 2025, 47% of callback interviews resulted in offers for summer 2026 positions, a decrease of two percentage points from the previous recruiting cycle.
Since 2023, offer rates have fallen below the historical range of 50-58% observed from 2014-2022.
In 2025, the acceptance rate increased by three percentage points, growing to a new record high of 52%.
This is the third consecutive year of record acceptance rates.

kp.k: Recruitment channels differed in offer and acceptance rates
kp.d: Employer-sponsored recruitment had a higher offer rate than school-sponsored recruitment, at 49% versus 39%. The ordering reversed for acceptance: school-sponsored offers were accepted at 55%, compared with 51% for employer-sponsored offers.
qs: By method, offer rates were higher for employer sponsored recruiting (49%) as compared to law school sponsored recruiting (39%).
However, offer acceptance rates were higher for offers that resulted from law school sponsored methods (55%) as compared to employer sponsored (51%).

kp.k: Total offers were flat; median office offers hit low
kp.d: Total offer volume for summer 2026 2L programs increased by only 0.4% compared with the previous recruitment cycle. The median number of offers per office fell to an all-time low of four. These measures describe aggregate offer volume and its office-level median, respectively, rather than completed hires.
qs: Overall, total offer volume for summer 2026 2L programs was essentially flat, increasing by just 0.4% as compared to the prior recruiting cycle.
The median number of 2L 2026 summer program offers extended per office was four, an all-time low.
